intent.raw_query: Vietnam on $800, backpacking 10 days, street food and culture, April 2026

experiences.name: Hanoi Old Quarter Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Wander through the maze-like streets of Hanoi's Old Quarter sampling iconic Vietnamese dishes including Bun Cha, Banh Mi, Pho, and Egg Coffee. Join a local-led walking tour or explore independently, hopping between street stalls and tiny plastic-stool restaurants packed with locals.

experiences.name: Hoi An Ancient Town Lantern Festival & Night Market
experiences.description: Explore the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town of Hoi An on foot, visiting centuries-old merchant houses, temples, and the iconic Japanese Covered Bridge. Stay for the monthly lantern festival or nightly market, sampling local specialties like Cao Lau and White Rose dumplings from street vendors along the Thu Bon River.

experiences.name: Halong Bay Budget Overnight Cruise
experiences.description: Board an affordable overnight junk boat cruise through the dramatic limestone karsts and emerald waters of Halong Bay. Includes kayaking through hidden caves and grottos, swimming stops, and a seafood dinner on deck. A quintessential backpacker experience that is breathtaking yet accessible on a tight budget.

experiences.name: Hue Imperial Citadel & Royal Tomb Bicycle Tour
experiences.description: Rent a bicycle and ride through the historic former imperial capital of Hue, exploring the massive 19th-century Imperial Citadel, the Forbidden Purple City ruins, and ornate royal tombs of the Nguyen Dynasty scattered along the Perfume River. A deeply immersive cultural journey into Vietnam's dynastic past.

experiences.name: Ho Chi Minh City Ben Thanh Market & District 1 Street Food Crawl
experiences.description: Dive into the sensory overload of Ben Thanh Market for fresh produce and local snacks, then hit the surrounding streets of District 1 for a self-guided street food crawl. Must-tries include Banh Xeo (sizzling crepes), Hu Tieu noodle soup, fresh spring rolls, and sugarcane juice. End the night at the lively Bui Vien backpacker street.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Vietnam
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at 13:00, clear customs and immigration. Take a budget airport bus or shared shuttle to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with a slow walk along the beachfront to shake off travel fatigue. Pick up a local SIM card from a nearby convenience store for cheap data (~50,000 VND).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll the nearest local night market or beach promenade. Explore the surrounding streets on foot to get a feel for the neighborhood. Watch the sunset from the beach if weather permits.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick snack at the airport arrival hall
meals.lunch: Grab a bánh mì sandwich from a street vendor near the airport or bus stop (~25,000–35,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Find a local com tam (broken rice) or pho stall near the resort for an authentic and affordable first dinner (~50,000–80,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light. Priority is rest and orientation. Exchange some USD to VND at the airport or a local bank for a fair rate. Avoid taxi touts — use Grab app for safe, metered rides.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and explore the local beach at sunrise. Walk along the shoreline and observe local fishermen bringing in their morning catch. Visit a nearby wet market to see fresh produce, seafood, and local life in full swing — a great cultural immersion experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local pagoda or temple in the area for a dose of Vietnamese spiritual culture (free entry). Wander the old quarter or town center if nearby, browsing local handicraft shops and souvenir stalls. Try a Vietnamese iced coffee (cà phê sữa đá) at a sidewalk café (~15,000–25,000 VND).
day_by_day.evening: Join a free or low-cost walking tour of the local neighborhood (many hostels and guesthouses organize these). Enjoy the vibrant street food scene after dark — try grilled skewers, fresh spring rolls, and local snacks from roadside vendors.

meals.breakfast: Bánh mì ốp la (baguette with fried egg) from a street cart near the resort (~20,000–30,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Bowl of bún bò Huế or phở at a local noodle shop (~40,000–60,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Street food dinner at the night market — mix of grilled corn, nem nướng, and fresh fruit (~60,000–100,000 VND total)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes. Carry a small daypack with water and sunscreen. Most pagodas require modest dress — bring a light scarf or sarong.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle or motorbike (50,000–100,000 VND/day) and explore the countryside or coastal roads around the resort area. Stop at scenic viewpoints and small villages along the way for authentic local interactions and photo opportunities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local fishing village to learn about traditional Vietnamese coastal life. Watch fishermen repair nets, see colorful basket boats (thuyền thúng), and if lucky, witness a fresh catch being sorted and sold. This is a deeply cultural and photogenic experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to town for a cooking class or simply replicate local flavors by shopping at a market and assembling your own Vietnamese-style picnic on the beach. Alternatively, find a rooftop bar with cheap local beer (bia hơi ~10,000–15,000 VND per glass).

meals.breakfast: Xôi (sticky rice with toppings) from a street vendor (~20,000–35,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood at a local beach shack — grilled fish or clams with rice (~80,000–120,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Bia hơi corner dinner with grilled meats and vegetables (~80,000–100,000 VND including drinks)

day_by_day.notes: If renting a motorbike, carry your passport or a copy. Drive on the right side of the road and wear a helmet at all times — it's both the law and essential safety.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to the nearest major cultural or historical site — a UNESCO heritage town, ancient citadel, or hill tribe market depending on the region. Depart early by local bus or shared minivan to maximize time (bus fares typically 30,000–80,000 VND).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the heritage site thoroughly — walk the ancient streets, visit museums (entry ~30,000–50,000 VND), and admire traditional architecture. Shop for handmade crafts, lacquerware, or silk at local artisan workshops where prices are more authentic than tourist shops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area by late afternoon or early evening. Wind down with a foot massage at a local spa (often 100,000–150,000 VND for 30–60 minutes) — a budget backpacker staple in Vietnam.

meals.breakfast: Cháo (rice porridge) at the hotel or a nearby stall (~25,000–40,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Cao lầu or white rose dumplings if near Hội An, or local regional specialty at the heritage site (~50,000–80,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Back near the resort — try a local family-run restaurant for a set rice meal (cơm phần) (~60,000–90,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Book shared transport the night before from your guesthouse or a local travel desk to get the best rates. Avoid private taxis for day trips — they are significantly more expensive.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning at the beach for a relaxed start. Join a free yoga session on the beach if offered by the resort, or simply swim and relax. This is a good day to do laundry (laundry services near backpacker areas cost ~20,000–30,000 VND per kg).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local art gallery, cultural center, or museum in the area to deepen your understanding of Vietnamese history and traditions. Many smaller regional museums have free or very low-cost entry (~20,000–30,000 VND). Look for exhibits on the Vietnam War, Cham culture, or local ethnic minorities.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Vietnamese performance if available locally — water puppetry, tuồng (classical opera), or folk music shows. Tickets are typically 80,000–150,000 VND and offer exceptional cultural value.

meals.breakfast: Bánh cuốn (steamed rice rolls) with pork and herbs (~30,000–45,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Self-assembled meal from the local market — fresh fruit, bánh mì, and coconut water (~40,000–60,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Pre-show street food near the performance venue — bún thịt nướng (grilled pork noodle salad) (~45,000–65,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Mid-trip rest day is important for budget backpackers to recharge. Use this day to plan the second half of the trip, book onward transport if needed, and update your travel journal.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning street food tour — either self-guided or with a local guide (budget tours ~150,000–200,000 VND). Sample at least 5–6 different dishes from different vendors: phở, bánh xèo (sizzling crepes), chè (sweet dessert soup), and more. This is the highlight for street food lovers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local craft village or workshop — pottery, silk weaving, lantern making, or incense production depending on the region. Many offer free entry with the opportunity to try making crafts yourself. Great for cultural immersion and unique photos.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset boat ride or kayak along a local river, bay, or lagoon (~100,000–200,000 VND for shared tours). Watch the sky change colors over the water, a quintessential Vietnam experience.

meals.breakfast: Covered by the street food morning tour — multiple small tastings (~80,000–150,000 VND total)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the craft village — packed lunch or simple noodle dish at a local stall (~40,000–60,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Seafood hotpot (lẩu hải sản) shared with fellow travelers at a local restaurant (~120,000–180,000 VND per person)

day_by_day.notes: The street food tour works best on an empty stomach — skip a heavy breakfast. Bring cash in small denominations for street vendors. Most do not accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Hike or trek to a nearby natural attraction — a waterfall, viewpoint, national park trail, or rice terrace depending on the region. Start early to beat the heat. Entrance fees for national parks are typically 40,000–80,000 VND. Bring plenty of water and snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the trek or return and visit a local ethnic minority village if in a highland area, or explore a mangrove forest or coral reef area if on the coast. Interact respectfully with locals and learn about their traditions and daily life.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort tired but fulfilled. Treat yourself to a cold local beer and dinner at a casual open-air restaurant. Share stories with other backpackers at the resort or a nearby hostel common area.

meals.breakfast: Early bánh mì or sticky rice packed for the trail (~25,000–35,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or simple meal at a trailhead or village stall (~40,000–70,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Relaxed dinner at a local restaurant — lemongrass chicken or tofu stir fry with rice (~70,000–100,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy shoes and light, breathable clothing for the hike. Leech socks are useful in forested areas during wet season. Always inform your accommodation of your trekking plans.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local Buddhist temple or pagoda complex for a peaceful morning. Arrive early to observe monks during morning prayers or chanting. Many temples offer free entry and a serene atmosphere perfect for reflection and photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local market focused on food and produce — not a tourist market, but where locals actually shop. Practice bargaining respectfully, try unfamiliar tropical fruits (dragon fruit, rambutan, longan), and pick up cheap snacks for the road.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost cultural event — a local festival, community gathering, or outdoor movie screening if happening. Alternatively, find a rooftop or beachside spot for stargazing and journaling with a cold drink in hand.

meals.breakfast: Hủ tiếu (southern-style noodle soup) at a local shop (~40,000–55,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Fresh market finds — grilled corn, steamed dumplings, fresh coconut (~50,000–70,000 VND assembled from stalls)
meals.dinner: Vegetarian Vietnamese dinner at a chay restaurant — filling and very affordable (~50,000–80,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Vegetarian (chay) restaurants are common in Vietnam and offer exceptional value — full meals for under 60,000 VND. Look for the Buddhist swastika symbol or 'Cơm Chay' signage.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day — spend the morning doing anything you missed or want to revisit. Alternatively, take a sunrise kayak or paddleboard session on the beach (~100,000–150,000 VND rental). Reflect on the journey and take final photos of the resort and surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Go souvenir shopping at local markets for gifts — lacquerware, silk scarves, coffee, dried fruits, and handmade goods. Budget 200,000–400,000 VND for a solid set of gifts. Avoid airport shops which are significantly overpriced. Pack your bag and settle any outstanding bills.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner with fellow travelers or solo at the best local restaurant you discovered during the trip. Splurge slightly on this final night — a full Vietnamese feast with multiple dishes is still very affordable (~150,000–250,000 VND). Watch the beach one last time at night.

meals.breakfast: Bánh mì with multiple fillings — your favorite combination discovered during the trip (~30,000–45,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Revisit your favorite street food spot from earlier in the trip for a nostalgic last taste (~50,000–80,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Farewell feast — gỏi cuốn (fresh spring rolls), cá kho tộ (caramelized fish), rau muống xào tỏi (morning glory), and jasmine rice (~150,000–250,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Tip your favorite street food vendors and restaurant staff — even 10,000–20,000 VND is meaningful and appreciated. Leave a positive review for budget-friendly spots to help fellow backpackers.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early, do a final check of your room, and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Grab a quick breakfast near the hotel. Head to the airport with plenty of time — aim to arrive at least 2–3 hours before your flight for international departures.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time, spend any remaining time at the airport or a nearby café. Use up remaining VND on snacks, drinks, or last-minute souvenirs inside the departure terminal. Reflect on 10 incredible days of Vietnamese culture, food, and adventure.
day_by_day.evening: Board your departure flight with a full heart, a packed bag of memories, and hopefully a plan to return to Vietnam someday.

meals.breakfast: Final Vietnamese breakfast — xôi gà (sticky rice with chicken) or bánh mì from a street cart (~25,000–40,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Airport food or convenience store snacks using remaining VND (~60,000–100,000 VND)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport restaurant if time permits

day_by_day.notes: Keep some VND for airport transport and last meals. Most airports have currency exchange but rates are poor — spend down your cash beforehand. Double-check passport, boarding pass, and all belongings before leaving the hotel. Safe travels!

trip_options.title: Classic Vietnam Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and settle in.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and freshen up. Take a leisurely stroll along the beachfront to get oriented with the local surroundings. Explore the nearest coastal strip, pick up a local SIM card, and exchange currency at a nearby exchange booth.
day_by_day.evening: Wander the nearest night market or local street food lane close to the resort. Sample introductory Vietnamese street snacks like bánh mì and fresh spring rolls. Enjoy a relaxed first evening soaking in the atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bowl of phở or bún bò Huế from a local street stall near the resort after check-in.
meals.dinner: Explore a nearby night market — try grilled corn, bánh xèo (sizzling crepes), and fresh sugarcane juice from street vendors. Budget around 100,000–150,000 VND.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Jet lag may be a factor. Hydrate well and avoid overpacking the first evening. April weather in Vietnam can be warm and humid — bring light, breathable clothing.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a sunrise walk along the beach. Visit a nearby local market (chợ) to observe daily Vietnamese life — vendors selling fresh produce, herbs, and seafood. Try a bowl of cháo (rice porridge) or bánh cuốn (steamed rice rolls) from a market stall for an authentic breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a culturally significant site near the resort area — a local pagoda or communal house (đình làng). Hire a local guide or join a small group tour to learn about Vietnamese customs, architecture, and spiritual practices. Browse local craft shops for handmade souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a mid-range restaurant along the waterfront for a seafood dinner featuring locally caught fish, grilled prawns, and morning glory stir-fry. Enjoy Vietnamese iced tea (trà đá) with your meal.

meals.breakfast: Bánh cuốn or cháo trắng from the local morning market — around 30,000–50,000 VND.
meals.lunch: Cơm tấm (broken rice with grilled pork) from a local eatery — around 50,000–80,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Seafood dinner at a mid-range beachfront restaurant — budget around 200,000–350,000 VND per person.

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly when visiting pagodas — cover shoulders and knees. Bring small denominations of VND for market purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Join a local cooking class offered in the area. Learn to prepare 3–4 classic Vietnamese dishes such as gỏi cuốn (fresh spring rolls), canh chua (sour soup), and chả giò (fried spring rolls). Classes typically include a market visit to source fresh ingredients.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby historical or cultural landmark — a French colonial building, museum, or heritage site depending on the region. Take time to read about the local history and interact with locals. Visit a traditional Vietnamese coffee shop for a cà phê trứng (egg coffee) or cà phê sữa đá (iced milk coffee).
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Vietnamese cultural performance if available locally (water puppetry, folk music, or a đờn ca tài tử music session). Dine at a family-run restaurant (quán ăn gia đình) for a home-style Vietnamese meal.

meals.breakfast: Included in the cooking class, or grab xôi (sticky rice) from a street cart — 20,000–40,000 VND.
meals.lunch: Lunch is typically included in the cooking class experience.
meals.dinner: Family-run Vietnamese restaurant — bún thịt nướng (grilled pork noodle salad) or cá kho tộ (caramelized fish in clay pot) — around 80,000–150,000 VND.

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class at least a day in advance. Most classes cost between 400,000–700,000 VND and are excellent value for mid-range budgets.

day_by_day.morning: Take a half-day excursion to a nearby nature spot — a river delta, rice paddy field, or forested hill depending on the region. Rent a bicycle or join a guided cycling tour through rural villages to experience authentic countryside Vietnam.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort area. Visit a local craft village if accessible — pottery, silk weaving, or lacquerware workshops where artisans demonstrate traditional techniques. Purchase handmade items directly from craftspeople.
day_by_day.evening: Street food crawl in the nearest town center. Try a variety of dishes: bún bò Huế, mì Quảng, nem lụi, and bánh bèo. Join locals at low plastic tables on the sidewalk for the full experience.

meals.breakfast: Bánh mì from a street cart — 25,000–45,000 VND. Vietnam's bánh mì is world-class and widely available.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from the cycling tour, or stop at a roadside quán for cơm bình dân (everyday rice set meal) — 50,000–70,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Street food crawl — budget 100,000–200,000 VND for a variety of small dishes and drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Cycling tours are a fantastic way to interact with locals. Wear sunscreen and a hat — April sun is strong. Carry cash for craft village purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated beach morning at the resort. Swim, relax, or try a water activity such as kayaking or snorkeling if available. This is a rest and recharge day mid-trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local neighborhood on foot with no fixed agenda — wander alleyways (hẻm), peek into local temples, chat with shopkeepers. Visit a Vietnamese pharmacy or herbal medicine shop for a cultural peek into traditional medicine.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar or beachside lounge. Enjoy a Saigon Beer or a fresh coconut while watching the sun dip below the horizon. Follow with dinner at a slightly elevated mid-range restaurant for a treat.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or a nearby café serving bánh mì ốp la (Vietnamese egg sandwich) — 40,000–60,000 VND.
meals.lunch: Light lunch — gỏi (Vietnamese salad) and chè (sweet dessert soup) from a local dessert stall — 50,000–80,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Mid-range restaurant with a set menu — lẩu (Vietnamese hot pot) for two is a great communal experience — 300,000–500,000 VND total.

day_by_day.notes: Day 5 is intentionally balanced with relaxation. Backpacking doesn't mean non-stop movement — pacing yourself ensures you enjoy the full 10 days.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a nearby UNESCO World Heritage Site or major cultural destination in the region (e.g., Hội An Ancient Town, Mỹ Sơn Sanctuary, or Huế Imperial Citadel depending on location). Depart early to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the heritage site. In Hội An, walk the lantern-lit streets, visit tailor shops, and cross the Japanese Covered Bridge. In Huế, tour the Imperial Citadel and royal tombs. In Mỹ Sơn, explore the ancient Cham ruins with a local guide.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Enjoy a quiet dinner and reflect on the day. Browse a local bookshop or art gallery if available.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort or a nearby café before departure.
meals.lunch: White Rose dumplings (bánh bao vạc) and Cao Lầu noodles in Hội An, or bún bò Huế in Huế — iconic regional dishes — 80,000–150,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Simple, comforting meal at a local quán — cháo gà (chicken rice porridge) or mì hoành thánh (wonton noodle soup) — 60,000–100,000 VND.

day_by_day.notes: Hire a reputable local guide at heritage sites for deeper cultural context — typically 200,000–400,000 VND for a half-day. Book transport the day before.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local fishing village or harbor early in the morning to watch fishermen return with their catch. This is a deeply authentic cultural experience. Purchase fresh seafood directly from fishermen if possible.
day_by_day.afternoon: Attend a Vietnamese language or calligraphy workshop — many cultural centers offer short 1–2 hour sessions for travelers. Learn to write your name in Vietnamese script or practice basic phrases. Visit a local temple festival if one is happening in the area (April is active for Vietnamese festivals).
day_by_day.evening: Join a street food tour led by a local guide. These tours typically cover 5–8 stops across different neighborhoods, covering dishes you might not discover on your own. Excellent for backpackers who want to eat like a local.

meals.breakfast: Bánh ướt (wet rice crepes) or hủ tiếu (southern noodle soup) from a harbor-side stall — 40,000–60,000 VND.
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch prepared at or near the fishing village — grilled fish, clams, and shrimp — 150,000–250,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Covered by the street food tour — budget 300,000–450,000 VND including guide fee and all tastings.

day_by_day.notes: Street food tours are one of the best investments in Vietnam. Look for tours run by local operators rather than large agencies for authenticity.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga or tai chi session on the beach (many resorts offer complimentary sessions, or join locals practicing in a nearby park). Follow with a visit to a local café district — Vietnam has a thriving coffee culture with unique regional styles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local market dedicated to textiles, spices, or handicrafts. Bargain respectfully for souvenirs — lacquerware, silk scarves, conical hats (nón lá), and hand-embroidered items make great gifts. Take a motorbike taxi (xe ôm) or ride-share app to explore a slightly farther neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a live music venue or cultural café hosting traditional Vietnamese music (nhạc dân tộc) or contemporary Vietnamese indie music. Many cities have vibrant evening cultural scenes. Pair with a light dinner and local craft beer.

meals.breakfast: Cà phê sữa đá and bánh mì at a local coffee shop — 50,000–80,000 VND. Try a specialty regional coffee if available.
meals.lunch: Bún chả (grilled pork with noodles) or phở bò (beef noodle soup) at a well-regarded local spot — 70,000–120,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Light dinner at a cultural café — gỏi cuốn, chả giò, and Vietnamese craft beer — 150,000–250,000 VND.

day_by_day.notes: Use Grab (Vietnam's dominant ride-share app) for safe and affordable transport. Download it before your trip. Tipping musicians at live venues is appreciated.

day_by_day.morning: Final full-day adventure: take a boat trip along a nearby river, bay, or lagoon. Options may include a Mekong Delta cruise, Ha Long Bay-style boat tour, or a local river excursion with stops at floating markets or river villages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from the boat trip. Spend the afternoon at leisure — final beach swim, resort spa treatment (many mid-range resorts offer affordable massages: 200,000–350,000 VND for 60 minutes), or a final round of souvenir shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory farewell dinner at the best mid-range restaurant you've discovered during the trip, or try a Vietnamese BBQ (nướng) restaurant where you grill your own meats and seafood at the table — a fun, social experience.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast to fuel the boat trip.
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood or local specialties served on the boat or at a riverside restaurant — typically included or available for 100,000–200,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Vietnamese BBQ farewell dinner — budget 250,000–400,000 VND per person including drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Book the boat trip at least 2 days in advance, especially during April which can be busy. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and motion sickness tablets if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — wake up early for one last sunrise on the beach. Take a slow walk, reflect on the journey, and capture final photos. Visit a nearby café for a leisurely Vietnamese breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the resort. Depending on departure time, visit any last-minute spots — a local bookshop for a Vietnamese cookbook, a pharmacy for herbal teas, or a final bowl of phở. Head to the airport or transport hub for onward travel.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. If the flight is late evening, enjoy a final Vietnamese meal at the airport or a nearby restaurant before boarding.

meals.breakfast: Slow, memorable breakfast at a favorite café discovered during the trip — cà phê trứng, bánh mì, and fresh fruit — 60,000–100,000 VND.
meals.lunch: Final bowl of phở or bún bò Huế at a trusted local spot — 70,000–120,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or a final meal near the departure terminal — budget 150,000–250,000 VND.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international flights for check-in and security. Keep some VND for last-minute purchases — leftover VND can be exchanged at the airport. Pack any liquid food items (fish sauce, sauces) in checked luggage.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Vietnam Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 - No morning activities scheduled. Rest and recover from flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, settle into your beachfront suite, and enjoy a welcome amenity. Take a leisurely stroll along the private beach to orient yourself with the resort surroundings.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's beachfront bar, followed by a relaxed welcome dinner at the resort's signature restaurant to ease into Vietnam time.

meals.breakfast: On the flight or at the airport lounge
meals.lunch: Light bites at the airport or during transfer
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort signature restaurant - fresh Vietnamese seafood tasting menu with premium local wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Flight LH arrives at 13:00. Allow 60-90 minutes for immigration, baggage claim, and private transfer to resort. Request early check-in in advance if possible. Ask the concierge to brief you on the 10-day itinerary and arrange all private transfers ahead of time.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise yoga session on the beach followed by a premium Vietnamese breakfast at the resort. Afterward, explore the local fishing village adjacent to the resort with a private guide to witness authentic coastal Vietnamese life and morning fish market activity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Chartered private boat excursion along the coastline, snorkeling in crystal-clear waters, and visiting hidden sea caves and secluded beaches inaccessible by land. Enjoy a gourmet picnic lunch served on deck by your private guide.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort for spa treatment - signature Vietnamese herbal massage using local ingredients. Dinner at a premium beachside restaurant in the nearby town known for its fresh catch prepared in traditional central Vietnamese style.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast spread - bánh mì, phở, fresh tropical fruits, Vietnamese egg coffee, and international options
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic on private charter boat - fresh seafood, spring rolls, premium Vietnamese cold cuts
meals.dinner: Upscale local seafood restaurant - whole grilled fish with lemongrass, tiger prawns, and Vietnamese dipping sauces

day_by_day.notes: Book the private boat charter through the resort concierge the evening before. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and light layers. April weather in Vietnam is generally warm and pleasant along the coast.

day_by_day.morning: Private cultural immersion tour to a nearby UNESCO-listed heritage site or ancient temple complex. Enjoy a guided walk through centuries-old architecture with a local historian providing deep cultural context on Vietnamese dynasties and traditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Premium Vietnamese cooking class at a renowned local culinary school. Learn to prepare regional specialties including fresh rice paper rolls, regional noodle soups, and traditional desserts using locally sourced ingredients.
day_by_day.evening: Street food walking tour through the local town's night market with a private food guide. Sample authentic street food including bánh xèo (sizzling pancakes), bún bò (beef noodle soup), and chè (sweet dessert soups) paired with local craft beer.

meals.breakfast: In-room private breakfast butler service - Vietnamese-style congee, fresh fruit platter, Vietnamese drip coffee
meals.lunch: Enjoy dishes prepared during the cooking class in an elegant dining setting
meals.dinner: Curated street food tour - multiple tastings across 6-8 local street food vendors in the night market

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class typically lasts 3-4 hours including a market visit. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the evening street food tour. Carry small denominations of Vietnamese Dong for street food stalls even though the guide handles most payments.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise trek or motorbike ride through the surrounding countryside and rice paddies with a local guide. Visit a traditional Vietnamese family home for an authentic tea ceremony and insight into rural Vietnamese daily life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a premium local artisan workshop - lacquerware, silk weaving, or traditional pottery depending on the region. Participate in a hands-on craft session and select bespoke souvenirs crafted by master artisans.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Vietnamese water puppet show or live cultural performance at a local theater. Post-show, dine at a fine dining restaurant celebrated for its fusion of French colonial and Vietnamese culinary traditions.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet breakfast with made-to-order Vietnamese pho station
meals.lunch: Farm-to-table lunch at a countryside restaurant overlooking rice terraces - set menu of regional specialties
meals.dinner: Fine dining Vietnamese-French fusion restaurant - multi-course tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book the cultural performance tickets through the concierge in advance as popular shows sell out. The motorbike ride option requires a comfort level with local traffic; a private car alternative can be arranged. Dress modestly when visiting family homes and temples.

day_by_day.morning: Private helicopter or seaplane scenic flight over the coastline and surrounding landscape for breathtaking aerial views of Vietnam's natural beauty. Alternatively, a premium sunrise cruise on a traditional wooden junk boat with champagne breakfast on deck.
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury spa afternoon at the resort - full-body Vietnamese herbal wrap, hot stone massage, and facial using local botanical ingredients. Spend remaining time relaxing at the infinity pool overlooking the sea.
day_by_day.evening: Private beachside dinner set up exclusively for you by the resort - candlelit table on the sand, personalized menu curated by the executive chef, live acoustic Vietnamese music performance.

meals.breakfast: Champagne breakfast on the scenic cruise or helicopter experience
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the resort - fresh Vietnamese salads, grilled seafood skewers, tropical smoothies
meals.dinner: Private bespoke beachside dinner - 5-course personalized menu with premium wine and fresh seafood

day_by_day.notes: The private beachside dinner must be booked at least 48 hours in advance with the resort. The helicopter or seaplane experience is weather-dependent; confirm availability with the concierge. This is an ideal day to recharge mid-trip.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip departure by private vehicle to a nearby UNESCO World Heritage City (such as Hội An or Huế depending on resort location). Morning exploration of the ancient town with a private cultural guide, visiting historic merchant houses, temples, and covered bridges.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the heritage city - visit the Imperial Citadel or ancient trading ports. Browse high-end local boutiques for custom-tailored silk garments made by master tailors (a 24-hour turnaround is often available in Hội An).
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at one of the heritage city's most acclaimed restaurants before returning to the resort by private car. Experience regional specialties unique to this area such as cao lầu noodles or white rose dumplings.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Premium lunch at a celebrated restaurant in the heritage city - regional set menu in a beautifully restored colonial building
meals.dinner: Award-winning restaurant in the heritage city known for authentic regional Vietnamese cuisine

day_by_day.notes: This is a full-day excursion; depart by 7:30 AM to maximize time. If visiting a tailor, bring reference photos and allow time for fittings. The return drive may take 1-2 hours depending on location. Comfortable walking shoes are essential for cobblestone streets.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding session in a nearby lagoon or bay. Explore mangrove forests and hidden inlets with a professional guide. Return to resort for a freshly prepared Vietnamese breakfast smoothie and light snack.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cultural immersion experience - join a local family for a traditional Vietnamese home-cooking session in their residence, learning recipes passed down through generations. Tour their herb garden and understand the philosophy of Vietnamese food culture.
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop or elevated dining experience at a premium restaurant with panoramic views of the coastline. Order the chef's selection of Vietnamese tapas-style dishes accompanied by premium Vietnamese wine or craft cocktails infused with local herbs.

meals.breakfast: Post-water activity light breakfast at the resort beach club
meals.lunch: Home-cooked Vietnamese family lunch as part of the cultural immersion experience
meals.dinner: Rooftop fine dining restaurant - panoramic coastal views, Vietnamese tapas menu, artisanal cocktail pairing

day_by_day.notes: The kayaking session is best done in the early morning before the sun becomes intense. The home-cooking experience is a highly personal and intimate activity - confirm details and any dietary restrictions with the concierge in advance. Tip the family generously as a gesture of appreciation.

day_by_day.morning: Guided visit to a premium local coffee plantation or tea estate (Vietnam is one of the world's top coffee producers). Learn about the cultivation and processing of Vietnamese coffee, including the famous weasel coffee (cà phê chồn), with a full tasting session.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a traditional Vietnamese market with a private guide and personal shopper. Select premium local products including silk, lacquerware, hand-embroidered items, and specialty food products. The guide ensures authentic quality and fair pricing.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private traditional music performance - featuring đàn bầu (monochord), đàn tranh (zither), or a full ensemble of Vietnamese classical instruments arranged exclusively through the resort. Follow with a refined dinner at the resort's premium restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast - Vietnamese egg coffee and bánh mì station
meals.lunch: Lunch at a celebrated local restaurant near the market - fresh Vietnamese noodle dishes and regional specialties
meals.dinner: Resort premium restaurant - Vietnamese royal cuisine inspired by imperial court recipes

day_by_day.notes: The private music performance can often be arranged through the local cultural department or resort concierge and typically lasts 45-60 minutes. Purchase vacuum-sealed specialty Vietnamese coffee as a premium souvenir. Bargaining is expected at markets but do so respectfully.

day_by_day.morning: Premium cycling tour through local villages, rice paddies, and rural landscapes with a knowledgeable guide. Stop at a local pagoda for a moment of reflection and cultural understanding of Vietnamese Buddhism. Visit a local school or community project as a meaningful cultural exchange.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to resort for a final luxury spa session - choose from a Vietnamese detox treatment, bamboo massage, or couples' spa ritual. Spend the remaining afternoon at leisure - swimming, reading on the beach, or enjoying the resort's premium amenities.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell street food adventure - a premium curated street food experience in the local town visiting the best vendors for one final immersive taste of authentic Vietnamese cuisine. End the evening with Vietnamese iced coffee and dessert at a charming local café.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before cycling tour
meals.lunch: Authentic local lunch at a village restaurant during the cycling tour - simple, fresh, and deeply traditional Vietnamese food
meals.dinner: Premium curated street food farewell tour - best of local street food with a private guide, ending at a rooftop café

day_by_day.notes: Rent premium e-bikes if a full cycling tour feels too strenuous. The farewell street food tour is a wonderful way to contrast the luxury resort experience with authentic grassroots Vietnamese culture - a highlight of any backpacker-inspired premium trip. Pack light for the cycling tour.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk on the beach or a peaceful meditation session arranged by the resort. Enjoy a leisurely and indulgent final breakfast at the resort, savoring every last Vietnamese flavor. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time - either a final relaxing pool session, last-minute shopping for premium Vietnamese souvenirs (lacquerware, silk scarves, specialty teas, artisan coffee), or a short visit to a nearby viewpoint for a final panoramic memory of Vietnam.
day_by_day.evening: Private luxury transfer to the airport. Enjoy the airport lounge before your departure flight. Reflect on an extraordinary 10-day journey through Vietnam's culture, cuisine, and coastal beauty.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell resort breakfast - full Vietnamese and international spread, premium Vietnamese drip coffee ceremony
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort or a farewell meal at a favorite restaurant from the trip
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or an early dinner before the flight

day_by_day.notes: Request a late checkout from the resort (usually until 14:00-16:00 for premium guests) to maximize your final day. Confirm airport transfer timing with the concierge the evening before. Declare any food items purchased as souvenirs at customs. Keep a small amount of Vietnamese Dong for tips and last-minute purchases.
